plan: With a private value of $25, I want to maximize potential profit. Since values are uniformly drawn between $0-$49, other bidders might have values around $25 too. A pure dominant strategy is impossible. I'll aim to bid slightly above my value but not excessively high. A bid around $30 gives me a reasonable chance of winning while limiting potential losses if I overbid. This strategy balances winning probability with risk management.

My value is $3, which is quite low. In a first-price sealed bid auction with values uniformly distributed between $0-$49, rational strategy suggests bidding below my true value. Since other bidders will likely bid strategically, I'll bid modestly to avoid overpaying. A bid around $2 represents a balanced approach - low enough to minimize potential loss, but competitive enough to have a small chance of winning if other bidders have similarly low values.

In a single-round auction with values drawn between $0-$49, the optimal strategy is to bid just above my expected second-price bid. My value is $26. Other rational bidders will likely bid near their own values. I'll aim to bid around $25-$27 to maximize winning probability while minimizing overpayment. This balanced approach gives me a good chance of winning without significantly reducing potential profit if I win.
